root.summary: A full-bleed magazine header, no rail — for a doc that wants to open with a statement, not a table of contents.

nodes.title: This is hero
nodes.tagline: layout:"hero" — a full-bleed gradient title, no fixed left rail.

blocks.text: Set "layout": "hero" and the doc opens with a large gradient-text heading and a wide, centered column below it — good for a proposal, an announcement, or anything that wants to lead with a statement instead of a nav tree.
Breadcrumb and search still work here, exactly as they do in the classic left-nav shell and in no-nav — they're decoupled from the sidebar, not tied to it.
Every layout mode shares the same node/blocks/primitives underneath — only the shell CSS changes. Copy this file's "layout" field into your own source.json to start a hero doc.
